name: How Do I Compare Remodeling Estimates for Cosmetic Versus Layout Changes?

mainEntity.name: How can I tell whether a kitchen remodeling estimate is for a cosmetic update or a full layout change?
mainEntity.text: How can I tell whether a kitchen remodeling estimate is for a cosmetic update or a full layout change?

acceptedAnswer.text: Two estimates may use the phrase “kitchen remodel” while describing very different projects. A cosmetic update may include painting, refacing, new countertops, hardware, backsplash, lighting, and fixtures in existing locations. A layout change can involve cabinet relocation, moved plumbing, new circuits, gas or ventilation work, wall removal, structural review, flooring replacement, and permit coordination. Ask each contractor to mark which walls, utilities, appliances, and cabinets remain in place. Confirm whether the estimate includes engineering or design coordination for removed walls, relocation of plumbing or gas, electrical-panel capacity, ducting, flooring repairs, and transitions into adjacent rooms. Check whether demolition and reconstruction of affected surfaces are included. Use the same layout plan when comparing bids. If one contractor proposes a cosmetic solution and another prices a reconfiguration, the totals should not be compared as competing prices. Ask for separate options if the decision is not final: an existing-layout option and a revised-layout option. This shows the incremental cost of improvements and helps align the budget with the desired result.
acceptedAnswer.description: A cosmetic estimate typically covers finishes, cabinet fronts, countertops, fixtures, or paint without relocating major services. A layout-change estimate should address walls, plumbing, electrical, ventilation, flooring transitions, structural review, permits, and design coordination. Confirm the category in writing.
